sentences.text:
By way of this application, the applicant - org. complainant under the provisions of Section 439(2)
of the Code of Criminal Procedure, seeks to cancel the bail granted by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court as per order dated 30/01/2023 passed in CR.MA No.1384 of 2023 in connection with FIR being C.R.No. I11191066220360 of 2022 registered with Vasana Police Station, for the offence punishable under Sections 354(A)(1)(i), 363, 366, 368, 506 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 7, 8, 11(6), 12 and 17 of the POCSO Act on the ground that accused- respondent no.2 committed breach of conditions no.(a) and (b) imposed while enlarging him on bail.

2. The short facts of the case are that FIR supra came to be registered against the accused wherein he came to be enlarged on regular bail by the co-ordinate Bench as per order dated 30/01/2023 passed in CR.MA No.1384 of 2023 while imposing following conditions:
Mamtaben

sentences.text: 3. Learned Advocate Ms.Chauhan for the petitioner would submit that accused-respondent no.2 is a habitual offender as he is committing one after another offence of similar nature.

She would submit that after the accused released on regular bail while imposing conditions supra by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court, he found to have been involved in such similar offence again with the victim of the case for which FIR came to be registered with the Ghatlodiya Police Station being FIR No.11191044230395 of 2023 for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376 [2] [n], 354[a],
354[d] & 114 of the Indian Penal Code and U/s 3 ja], 4, 5 [1], 6, 7, 8, 11[4], 12, 16 & 18 of the POCSO Act, 2012.

3.1 Learned Advocate Ms.Chauhan would further submit that after registration of the said offence,
the accused preferred regular bail application before the learned trial Court which came to be rejected as per order dated 03/02/2024 passed in CR.MA No.242 of 2024.
She would furthers submit that first FIR came to be lodged by the mother of the victim whereas the second FIR came to be lodged by the aunt of the victim.

She would therefore submit that as the accused is found to have been repeatedly involved in the heinous offence by committing breach of conditions imposed while enlarging on bail, which would indicate that he has shown total disregard to the order NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/1032/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined passed by this Hon'ble Court and therefore the bail of the accused may be cancelled.
4. On the other hand, learned Advocate for the respondent no.2-org. accused would submit that the victim was in love relationship with the accused.
He would further submit that background of the dispute is altogether different which has been given criminal colour.
He would therefore submit to dismiss the application.

5. Learned APP would submit that since the accused is found to have indulged in similar offence by committing breach of conditions imposed while enlarging him on bail and when the bail application for the second FIR also came to be rejected by the learned trial Court, this Court may also cancel the bail granted to the accused in the first offence.
He would therefore submit that considering the facts and circumstances of the case appropriate order may be passed.

6. Having heard the learned Advocates for the rival sides, it is an undisputed fact that accused is found to have been repeatedly involved in heinous offence punishable under the POCSO Act by committing breach of conditions imposed upon him while enlarging on bail; with the same victim.
To be noted that, at the time of grating bail in respect of first FIR, the age of the victim is 14 years and 10 months and therefore specific conditions was imposed by the co-operate Bench of this Court.
However, ignoring such bail condition, the accused is found to have been committed another offence with the said victim who is aged 16 months and 08 months.
Thus, the accused is habitual NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/1032/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined of committing such offence and therefore no leniency should be shown to him.

Paragarph 18 is relevant which reads thus:
"18.

The offence alleged in the instant case is heinous and would be a onslaught on the dignity of the womanhood and the age old principle of            
         
         
        
          
         
         
        
     (where women are respected Gods live there)

would recede to the background and the guilty not being punished by process of law or accused persons are allowed to move around freely in the society or in spite of there being prima facie material being present they are allowed to move around freely in the society before guilt is proved and are likely to indulge in either threatening the prosecution witnesses or inducing them in any manner to jettison the criminal justice system

, then the superior court will have to necessarily step in to undo the damage occasioned due to erroneous orders being passed by courts below."
8.
For the foregoing reasons, the present petition deserves to be allowed and accordingly it is allowed.
The regular bail granted to the respondent no.2 - org.
Accused in connection with the FIR being C.R.No. I11191066220360 of 2022 registered with Vasana Police Station stands cancelled.
